## Overview
Comparative scouting analysis of the New England Patriots and 
Los Angeles Rams using NFL play-by-play data, built entirely in R and Quarto.

## Metrics Analyzed
- Pass/run rate splits
- Snaps from shotgun vs under center
- 4th down conversion tendencies
- Goal-to-go situational analysis

## Tools / Packages Used
- nflreadr
- tidyverse
- ggplot2
- flextable
- patchwork



# Loading Packages

```{r setup, echo=TRUE, output=FALSE}
# packages
library(tidyverse)
library(rvest)
library(nflreadr)
library(janitor)
library(descr)
library(flextable)
library(patchwork)
```

# Task 1 - NFL Scouting Reports

```{r, echo=TRUE, output=FALSE}
# loading the data
pbp <- load_pbp(2025)
```


```{r}
# creating the variables
pbp <- pbp |> 
  mutate(    dome = case_when (
    roof== "dome" ~ 1,
    roof== "closed" ~ 1,
    roof== "outdoors" ~ 0,
    roof== "open" ~ 0), 
    wind_group = case_when(
      wind >= 0 & wind <= 2 ~ "no breeze",
      dome ==1 ~ "no breeze",
      wind >= 3 & wind <= 7 ~ "light breeze",
      wind >= 8 & wind <= 14 ~ "moderate breeze",
      wind >= 15 & wind <= 25 ~ "strong breeze",
      wind > 25 ~ "strong gusts",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_), 
    wind_speed = if_else(dome==0, wind, 0), 
    fg_distance=yardline_100+17, 
    fg_group = case_when(
      fg_distance < 30  ~ "<30",
      fg_distance >= 30 & fg_distance <= 39 ~ "30-39",
      fg_distance >= 40 & fg_distance <= 44 ~ "40-44",
      fg_distance >= 45 & fg_distance <= 49 ~ "45-49",
      fg_distance >= 50 & fg_distance <= 55 ~ "50-55",
      fg_distance > 55 & fg_distance <= 60  ~ "55-60",
      fg_distance > 60   ~ "60+",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_), 
    fg_50_plus = if_else(fg_distance >49, 1, 0),  
    fg_long = if_else(fg_distance >54, 1, 0),  
    fg_made = case_when(
      field_goal_result == "made" ~ 1,
      field_goal_result == "missed" ~ 0,
      field_goal_result == "blocked" ~ 0,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_  ), 
    field_position_group = case_when(
      yardline_100 <=10 ~ "inside 10",
      yardline_100 >10 & yardline_100 <= 20 ~ "red zone",
      yardline_100 > 20 & yardline_100 <= 45 ~ "driving zone",
      yardline_100 > 45 & yardline_100 <= 55 ~ "midfield",
      yardline_100 > 55 & yardline_100 <= 80 ~ "opp zone",
      yardline_100 > 80 & yardline_100 <= 95 ~ "opp red zone",
      yardline_100 > 95 & yardline_100 <= 99 ~ "inside opp 5",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_), 
    drive_points = case_when(
      fixed_drive_result == "Touchdown" ~ 7,
      fixed_drive_result == "Field goal" ~ 3,
      fixed_drive_result == "Safety" ~ -2,
      fixed_drive_result == "Opp touchdown" ~ -7,
      TRUE ~ 0), 
    to_go = case_when(
      ydstogo == 1 ~ 1,
      ydstogo %in% 2:3 ~ 2,
      ydstogo %in% 4:6 ~ 3,
      ydstogo %in% 7:9 ~ 4,
      ydstogo %in% 10:14 ~ 5,
      ydstogo >= 15 ~ 6,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_ ),
    to_go_f = factor(to_go, 
                     levels = 1:6, 
                     labels = c("1 yard", "2-3 yards", "4-6 yards", "7-9 yards", "10-14 yards", "15+ yards")))
```



```{r}
# specific dataframes for first half only

# All Team's Deep Dive on Passing Tendencies in First Half
rate_all <- pbp |> 
  filter(
    down %in% 1:3,
    game_seconds_remaining > 1799,
    pass_attempt %in% c(0,1) | rush_attempt %in% c(0,1),
    goal_to_go==0
  ) |> 
  group_by(down, to_go_f) |> 
  summarise(
    pass_percent = mean(pass_attempt, na.rm = TRUE),
    pass_att = sum(pass_attempt, na.rm = TRUE),
    plays = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

rate_all.plot <- ggplot(rate_all, aes(x = to_go_f, y = factor(down), fill = pass_percent)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = paste0(
      scales::percent(pass_percent, accuracy = 1), "\n(",
      plays, ")")),
    color = "black",
    lineheight = 0.9,
    size = 4) +
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "antiquewhite",
    high = "#46b478",
    labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(x = "Yards to Go",
       y = "Down",
       fill = "Pass %",
       title = "NFL Probability of Passing by Down and Distance (2025)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(axis.title.y = element_text(angle = 0, vjust = 0.5),
        panel.grid = element_blank())

# check
# rate_all.plot

```

# 1.1 Pass/Run Rates
```{r}
rate_all.plot / pats.rate.plot
```
Based on comparison to NFL 2025 metrics, the New England Patriots seem to be predictable
for these scenarios:

On 2nd down and 1 yard to go, the Patriots prefer to run the ball (13% pass rate vs NFL average of 28%)
On 2nd down and 10-14 yards to to, the Patriots prefer to pass (76% vs NFL average of 64%)

```{r}
rate_all.plot / rams.rate.plot
```
Based on comparison to NFL 2025 metrics, the LA Rams seem to be more evenly balanced
compared to the New England Patriots. 

One scenario that stands out is 2nd down and 10-14 yards to go. Here, the LA Rams
prefer to pass the ball (78% vs 64% NFL average)

## 1.2 Snaps from shotgun or under center

```{r}
# All NFL snaps
snaps_all <- pbp |> 
  filter(
    down %in% 1:3,
    game_seconds_remaining > 1799,
    pass_attempt %in% c(0,1) | rush_attempt %in% c(0,1),
    goal_to_go==0) %>%
  group_by(down, to_go_f, shotgun) |> 
  summarise(
    pass_percent = mean(pass_attempt, na.rm = TRUE),
    pass_att = sum(pass_attempt, na.rm = TRUE),
    plays = n(),
    .groups = "drop")

snaps_all.plot <-  ggplot(snaps_all, aes(x = to_go_f, y = factor(down), fill = pass_percent)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(
      scales::percent(pass_percent, accuracy = 1), "\n(",plays, ")")),
    color = "black",
    lineheight = 0.9,
    size = 4) +
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "antiquewhite",
    high = "#46b478",
    labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  facet_wrap(~ shotgun, nrow = 1,
             labeller = labeller(
               shotgun = c(`0` = "Under Center", `1` = "Shotgun"))) +
  labs(x = "Yards to Go",
    y = "Down",
    fill = "Pass %",
    title = "NFL Probability of Passing by Down, Distance & Formation (2025)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 12)) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8, angle = 45)) + 
  theme(axis.title.y = element_text(angle = 0, 
                                    vjust = 0.5,
                                    ),
    panel.grid = element_blank())

# check
# snaps_all.plot 
```

```{r}
snaps_all.plot
snaps_all.pats.plot
```
The heatmaps show that both the Patriots and Rams use the shotgun formation more 
than under center overall. 

For 1st down and 10-14 yards to go, Patriots are more likely to pass when using
the shotgun formation (64% pass rate compared to NFL's 59% pass rate)

For 2nd down and 7-9 yards to go, Patriots are more likely to run the ball
when using under center formation (30% pass rate compared to NFL's 44% pass rate)

For 3rd down and 2-3 yards to go, Patriots are more likely to pass the ball
when using shotgun formation (69% pass rate compare to NFL's 59% pass rate)


```{r}
snaps_all.rams.plot
```
The LA rams seem to be more pass heavy on 2nd down from 4-6 yards (42% compared to NFL's 29%)
and on 2nd down & 7-9 yards (57% compared to NFL's 44%) for under center formation.

Overall LA seems to be more of a passing team compared to NFL averages when using Shotgun
formation. 

1st down & 10-14 yards to go, LA passes more than NFL (77% pass rate vs NFL's 59%)

2nd down & 10-14 yards to go, LA passes more than NFL (85% pass rate vs NFL's 69%)

3rd down & 2-3 yards to go, LA passes more than NFL (83% pass rate vs NFL's 59%)

3rd down & 4-6 yards to go, LA passes more than NF (92% pass rate vs NFL's 79%)

Compared to the Patriots, LA seems to pass the ball a lot more than average (from shotgun) 
and on 2nd down and 2 to 9 yards to go (under center). 
This is something opposing teams can take into account. 


## 1.3 Going for it on 4th Down

```{r}
fourth.all <-pbp |>  
    filter(down == 4,
    game_seconds_remaining > 1799,
    goal_to_go==0,
    fourth_down_failed ==1 | fourth_down_converted == 1
    ) |> 
 
  group_by(to_go_f) |>  
  summarise(pass_percent = mean(pass_attempt, na.rm = TRUE),
            Attempts=n())|> 
  mutate(Team = "NFL")

```


```{r}
# New England
fourth.pats <-pbp |>  
    filter(down == 4,
    posteam == "NE", # pats only
    game_seconds_remaining > 1799,
    goal_to_go==0,
    fourth_down_failed ==1 | fourth_down_converted == 1
    ) |> 
 
  group_by(to_go_f) |>  
  summarise(pass_percent = mean(pass_attempt, na.rm = TRUE),
            Attempts=n()) |> 
  mutate(Team = "Patriots")
```


```{r}
# Los Angeles 
fourth.rams <-pbp |>  
    filter(down == 4,
    posteam == "LA", # rams only
    game_seconds_remaining > 1799,
    goal_to_go==0,
    fourth_down_failed ==1 | fourth_down_converted == 1
    ) |> 
 
  group_by(to_go_f) |>  
  summarise(pass_percent = mean(pass_attempt, na.rm = TRUE),
            Attempts=n()) |> 
  mutate(Team = "Rams")

```


```{r}
fourth.combined <- bind_rows(fourth.all, fourth.pats, fourth.rams) |> 
  select(Team, everything()) 

fourth.combined |> 
  flextable() |> 
  set_header_labels(
    to_go_f = "Yards to Go",
    pass_percent = "Pass Rate"
  ) |>
  bg(i = ~ Team == "NFL", bg = "antiquewhite") |>
  bg(i = ~ Team == "Patriots", bg = "lightblue") |>
  bg(i = ~ Team == "Rams", bg = "#FFD100") |>
  bold(j = "Team") |>
  merge_v(j = "Team") |>
  valign(valign = "top", j = "Team") |>
  autofit()
```

Based on the table above:
1 yard to go - Both teams go for it (run the ball) as their pass rates are quite low and matches what
most teams in the NFL do

2 to 3 yards to go - Teams in the NFL are likely to pass as the average is close to 90%. Here, the 
Patriots are below the NFL average so can be expected to run the ball. For Rams, they most likely will
pass when going for it, but for the first half the sample sizes for both teams is quite low.


For Goal to go situations:
On 1st down & 7-9 yards to go, the Patriots are more likely to run the ball
(18% pass rate vs NFL's 29%)

On 2nd & 2-3 yards to go, the Patriots are more likely to pass the ball
(60% pass rate vs NFL's 41%)

On 3rd down & 2-3 yards to go, the Patriots are more likely to pass the ball
(100% pass rate vs NFL's 53%)


```{r}
rate_all.gtg.plot / rams.gtg.plot
```
For Goal to go situations:

On 2nd down & 1 yard to go, the LA Rams are more likely to pass the ball 
(71% pass rate vs NFL's 19%)

On 2nd & 3rd down with 7 to 14 yards to go, the LA Rams have passed the ball. 
However, these are all single attempts only for goal to go situations. 
As the previous analysis has shown that LA Rams are a pass oriented team and 
therefore they will have the tendency to pass rather than run the ball on 2nd and 3rd down
with more than 7 yards to go


```{r}
fourthAndGoal <- pbp |> 
  filter(
    down == 4,
    goal_to_go==1,
     posteam %in% c("NE", "LA") 
  ) |> 
  
  mutate( go.for.it = if_else(
    fourth_down_converted == 1 | fourth_down_failed == 1,
    1,0
  )
    ) |> 
  group_by(posteam) |>
  summarise(
    go.for.it.rate = mean(go.for.it, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) 

fourthAndGoal |> 
  flextable() |> 
  set_header_labels(
    posteam = "Team",
    go.for.it.rate = "Go For it Rate"
  ) |>
  autofit()
```

Based on the table above, the LA Rams seem to go for it slightly more than the Patriots given their
tendency on being a more pass oriented team
